Extend historical commemorations before the legacy 2000 cutoff: start anniversary rules at their origins (fromYear = anniversaryBase + 1) for 17 events, start the Paris Peace Agreement (1991) and Win-Win Policy Day (1998) at their signing years, and add 10 static milestones for original dates: Victory Day 1979-01-07, Independence 1953-11-09, Constitution 1993-09-24, Angkor UNESCO 1992-12-14, ICJ Preah Vihear 1962-06-15, UN membership 1955-12-14, UNESCO membership 1951-07-03, National Police 1945-05-16, Labor Day 1886-05-01, Human Rights Day 1948-12-10.

Correct royal commemoration start years: Coronation Day has been observed annually since the coronation on 29 October 2004 (was clamped at 2014, missing 2004-2013), and the King-Father commemoration was first observed on 15 October 2013, one year after his death (was clamped at 2014, missing 2013).

Apply event-origin research (docs/research dossiers): set 20 observances to verified first-observance years (international days 1948-1994 with Cambodia-first for Teachers 1997, Indigenous Peoples 2005 and Persons with Disabilities 1999; National Day of Remembrance moved to its 2018 statutory designation with a 1984 Day of Hatred milestone; Arbor Day from its 1992 revival; Fish Day 2003; Anti-Corruption 2004; Anti-Human-Trafficking 2007); split the combined World Water and World Meteorological Day into separate events (22 March since 1993, 23 March since 1961); model the pre-2002 International Day of Peace on the General Assembly opening day (third Tuesday, 1982-2001) with the documented 14 September 2001 exception; attach research provenance to the royal-day corrections.

Apply round-2 research (docs/research/round_2_*): National Environmental Sanitation Day starts at its founding instrument, Sub-decree No. 47 of 12 June 1995 (first observed 23 November 1995, replacing the unverified 2017 start); International Buddhist Day starts at 8 April 2025, the first Cambodian observance per the Ministry of Information (the 16 August 2024 sub-decree postdates that year’s 8 April); the pre-2002 International Day of Peace gains documented exceptions for 1998 (9 September, early GA-53 opening), 1999 (14 September, second-Tuesday GA-54 opening per SG/SM/7126) and 2000 (5 September, Millennium Assembly).

Queen Mother’s Birthday starts in 1994, the first calendar year of the restored Kingdom’s holiday schedule (monarchy restored 24 September 1993, after that year’s 18 June). The maintainer attests the official day has not been missed in any year, resolving the placeholder 2000 start; Gemini’s round-1/2 dossiers independently claim the 1994 restoration-era start.

Maintainer attests Win-Win Policy Day was commemorated every year through 2023, then renamed “Peace Day in Cambodia” and elevated to a national holiday from 29 December 2024 (Sub-decree No. 01 ANKr.BK of 1 January 2024 per docs/research). Rule bounds already matched (win-win 1998-2023, peace_day_cambodia from 2024); research provenance is now attached to both events.

Maintainer confirms 2026 is the 27th National Mine Awareness Day; counting back fixes anniversaryBase 1999 with the first observance on 24 February 2000, matching official usage (UNDP/CMAA 2024 = 25th). Values already matched; research provenance is attached to the event.

Maintainer endorses the Gemini round-2 account of the Day of Hatred: instituted by PRK National Assembly resolution in 1983 (adopted 18 August 1983 per TVK), first observed nationally on 20 May 1984, full official designation ទិវាចងកំហឹងចំពោះរបបប្រល័យពូជសាសន៍ ប៉ុល ពត អៀង សារី ខៀវ សំផន, shortened officially to ទិវាចងកំហឹង ២០ ឧសភា, and renamed ទិវាជាតិនៃការចងចាំ by Sub-decree No. 19 ANKr.BK in 2018 (settling the competing 2001 rename claim). Both endpoints already modeled correctly; the middle years 1985-2017 remain intentionally blank pending evidence of annual observance. No data change.
